/*
 * "test_override({name}, {val})" function
 */
    void
f_test_override(typval_T *argvars, typval_T *rettv UNUSED)
{
    char_u *name = (char_u *)"";
    int     val;
    static int save_starting = -1;

    if (check_for_string_arg(argvars, 0) == FAIL
		|| check_for_number_arg(argvars, 1) == FAIL)
	return;

    name = tv_get_string(&argvars[0]);
    val = (int)tv_get_number(&argvars[1]);

    if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"redraw") == 0)
	disable_redraw_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"redraw_flag") == 0)
	ignore_redraw_flag_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"char_avail") == 0)
	disable_char_avail_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"starting") == 0)
    {
	if (val)
	{
	    if (save_starting < 0)
		save_starting = starting;
	    starting = 0;
	}
	else
	{
	    starting = save_starting;
	    save_starting = -1;
	}
    }
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"nfa_fail") == 0)
	nfa_fail_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"syn_idlist_cache") == 0)
	disable_syn_idlist_cache_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"no_query_mouse") == 0)
	no_query_mouse_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"no_wait_return") == 0)
	no_wait_return = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"ui_delay") == 0)
	ui_delay_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"unreachable") == 0)
	ignore_unreachable_code_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"term_props") == 0)
	reset_term_props_on_termresponse = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"vterm_title") == 0)
	disable_vterm_title_for_testing = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"uptime") == 0)
	override_sysinfo_uptime = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"alloc_lines") == 0)
	ml_get_alloc_lines = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"autoload") == 0)
	override_autoload = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"defcompile") == 0)
	override_defcompile = val;
    else if (STRCMP(name, (char_u *)"ALL") == 0)
    {
	disable_char_avail_for_testing = FALSE;
	disable_redraw_for_testing = FALSE;
	ignore_redraw_flag_for_testing = FALSE;
	nfa_fail_for_testing = FALSE;
	disable_syn_idlist_cache_for_testing = FALSE;
	no_query_mouse_for_testing = FALSE;
	ui_delay_for_testing = 0;
	reset_term_props_on_termresponse = FALSE;
	override_sysinfo_uptime = -1;
	// ml_get_alloc_lines is not reset by "ALL"
	if (save_starting >= 0)
	{
	    starting = save_starting;
	    save_starting = -1;
	}
    }
    else
	semsg(_(e_invalid_argument_str), name);
}

/*
 * "test_refcount({expr})" function
 */
    void
f_test_refcount(typval_T *argvars, typval_T *rettv)
{
    int retval = -1;

    switch (argvars[0].v_type)
    {
	case VAR_UNKNOWN:
	case VAR_ANY:
	case VAR_VOID:
	case VAR_NUMBER:
	case VAR_BOOL:
	case VAR_FLOAT:
	case VAR_SPECIAL:
	case VAR_STRING:
	case VAR_INSTR:
	    break;

	case VAR_JOB:
#ifdef FEAT_JOB_CHANNEL
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_job != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_job->jv_refcount - 1;
#endif
	    break;
	case VAR_CHANNEL:
#ifdef FEAT_JOB_CHANNEL
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_channel != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_channel->ch_refcount - 1;
#endif
	    break;
	case VAR_FUNC:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_string != NULL)
	    {
		ufunc_T *fp;

		fp = find_func(argvars[0].vval.v_string, FALSE);
		if (fp != NULL)
		    retval = fp->uf_refcount;
	    }
	    break;
	case VAR_PARTIAL:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_partial != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_partial->pt_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_BLOB:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_blob != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_blob->bv_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_LIST:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_list != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_list->lv_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_TUPLE:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_tuple != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_tuple->tv_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_DICT:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_dict != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_dict->dv_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_CLASS:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_class != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_class->class_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_OBJECT:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_object != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_object->obj_refcount - 1;
	    break;
	case VAR_TYPEALIAS:
	    if (argvars[0].vval.v_typealias != NULL)
		retval = argvars[0].vval.v_typealias->ta_refcount - 1;
	    break;
    }

    rettv->v_type = VAR_NUMBER;
    rettv->vval.v_number = retval;

}

#ifdef FEAT_GUI
    static int
test_gui_drop_files(dict_T *args UNUSED)
{
# if defined(HAVE_DROP_FILE)
    int		row;
    int		col;
    int_u	mods;
    char_u	**fnames;
    int		count = 0;
    typval_T	t;
    list_T	*l;
    listitem_T	*li;

    if (!dict_has_key(args, "files")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "row")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "col")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "modifiers"))
	return FALSE;

    (void)dict_get_tv(args, "files", &t);
    row = (int)dict_get_number(args, "row");
    col = (int)dict_get_number(args, "col");
    mods = (int)dict_get_number(args, "modifiers");

    if (t.v_type != VAR_LIST || list_len(t.vval.v_list) == 0)
	return FALSE;

    l = t.vval.v_list;
    fnames = ALLOC_MULT(char_u *, list_len(l));
    if (fnames == NULL)
	return FALSE;

    FOR_ALL_LIST_ITEMS(l, li)
    {
	// ignore non-string items
	if (li->li_tv.v_type != VAR_STRING
		|| li->li_tv.vval.v_string == NULL)
	    continue;

	fnames[count] = vim_strsave(li->li_tv.vval.v_string);
	if (fnames[count] == NULL)
	{
	    while (--count >= 0)
		vim_free(fnames[count]);
	    vim_free(fnames);
	    return FALSE;
	}
	count++;
    }

    if (count > 0)
	gui_handle_drop(TEXT_X(col - 1), TEXT_Y(row - 1), mods, fnames, count);
    else
	vim_free(fnames);
# endif

    return TRUE;
}

    static int
test_gui_mouse_event(dict_T *args)
{
    int		button;
    int		row;
    int		col;
    int		repeated_click;
    int_u	mods;
    int		move;

    if (!dict_has_key(args, "row")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "col"))
	return FALSE;

    // Note: "move" is optional, requires fewer arguments
    move = (int)dict_get_bool(args, "move", FALSE);

    if (!move && (!dict_has_key(args, "button")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "multiclick")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "modifiers")))
	return FALSE;

    row = (int)dict_get_number(args, "row");
    col = (int)dict_get_number(args, "col");

    if (move)
    {
	int pY = row;
	int pX = col;
	// the "move" argument expects row and col coordnates to be in pixels,
	// unless "cell" is specified and is TRUE.
	if (dict_get_bool(args, "cell", FALSE))
	{
	    // calculate the middle of the character cell
	    // Note: Cell coordinates are 1-based from Vim script
	    pY = (row - 1) * gui.char_height + gui.char_height / 2;
	    pX = (col - 1) * gui.char_width + gui.char_width / 2;
	}
	gui_mouse_moved(pX, pY);
    }
    else
    {
	button = (int)dict_get_number(args, "button");
	repeated_click = (int)dict_get_number(args, "multiclick");
	mods = (int)dict_get_number(args, "modifiers");

	// Reset the scroll values to known values.
	// XXX: Remove this when/if the scroll step is made configurable.
	mouse_set_hor_scroll_step(6);
	mouse_set_vert_scroll_step(3);

	gui_send_mouse_event(button, TEXT_X(col - 1), TEXT_Y(row - 1),
							repeated_click, mods);
    }

    return TRUE;
}

    static int
test_gui_scrollbar(dict_T *args)
{
    char_u	*which;
    long	value;
    int		dragging;
    scrollbar_T *sb = NULL;

    if (!dict_has_key(args, "which")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "value")
	    || !dict_has_key(args, "dragging"))
	return FALSE;

    which = dict_get_string(args, "which", FALSE);
    value = (long)dict_get_number(args, "value");
    dragging = (int)dict_get_number(args, "dragging");

    if (STRCMP(which, "left") == 0)
	sb = &curwin->w_scrollbars[SBAR_LEFT];
    else if (STRCMP(which, "right") == 0)
	sb = &curwin->w_scrollbars[SBAR_RIGHT];
    else if (STRCMP(which, "hor") == 0)
	sb = &gui.bottom_sbar;
    if (sb == NULL)
    {
	semsg(_(e_invalid_argument_str), which);
	return FALSE;
    }
    gui_drag_scrollbar(sb, value, dragging);
# ifndef USE_ON_FLY_SCROLL
    // need to loop through normal_cmd() to handle the scroll events
    exec_normal(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE);
# endif

    return TRUE;
}

	    || check_for_dict_arg(argvars, 1) == FAIL
	    || argvars[1].vval.v_dict == NULL)
	return;

    event = tv_get_string(&argvars[0]);
    if (STRCMP(event, "dropfiles") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_drop_files(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
# if defined(FIND_REPLACE_DIALOG)
    else if (STRCMP(event, "findrepl") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_find_repl(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
# endif
# ifdef MSWIN
    else if (STRCMP(event, "key") == 0 || STRCMP(event, "mouse") == 0 || STRCMP(event, "set_keycode_trans_strategy") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_mswin_event(event, argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
# endif
    else if (STRCMP(event, "mouse") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_mouse_event(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
    else if (STRCMP(event, "scrollbar") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_scrollbar(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
    else if (STRCMP(event, "tabline") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_tabline_event(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
    else if (STRCMP(event, "tabmenu") == 0)
	rettv->vval.v_number = test_gui_tabmenu_event(argvars[1].vval.v_dict);
    else
    {
	semsg(_(e_invalid_argument_str), event);
	return;
    }
#endif
}

    void
f_test_settime(typval_T *argvars, typval_T *rettv UNUSED)
{
    if (in_vim9script() && check_for_number_arg(argvars, 0) == FAIL)
	return;

    time_for_testing = (time_t)tv_get_number(&argvars[0]);
}

#endif // defined(FEAT_EVAL)

 * Differences between version 5.8 and 6.x can be found with ":help version6".

 * Differences between version 3.0 and 4.x can be found with ":help version4".
 * All the remarks about older versions have been removed, they are not very
 * interesting.
 */

#include "version.h"

char		*Version = VIM_VERSION_SHORT;
static char	*mediumVersion = VIM_VERSION_MEDIUM;

#if defined(HAVE_DATE_TIME)
# if defined(VMS) && defined(VAXC)
char	longVersion[sizeof(VIM_VERSION_LONG_DATE) + sizeof(__DATE__)
						      + sizeof(__TIME__) + 3];

    void
init_longVersion(void)
{
    /*
     * Construct the long version string.  Necessary because
     * VAX C can't concatenate strings in the preprocessor.
     */
    strcpy(longVersion, VIM_VERSION_LONG_DATE);
#  ifdef BUILD_DATE
    strcat(longVersion, BUILD_DATE);
#  else
    strcat(longVersion, __DATE__);
    strcat(longVersion, " ");
    strcat(longVersion, __TIME__);
#  endif
    strcat(longVersion, ")");
}

# else
char	*longVersion = NULL;

    void
init_longVersion(void)
{
    if (longVersion != NULL)
	return;

#  ifdef BUILD_DATE
    char *date_time = BUILD_DATE;
#  else
    char *date_time = __DATE__ " " __TIME__;
#  endif
    char *msg = _("%s (%s, compiled %s)");
    size_t len = strlen(msg)
	+ STRLEN_LITERAL(VIM_VERSION_LONG_ONLY)
	+ STRLEN_LITERAL(VIM_VERSION_DATE_ONLY)
	+ strlen(date_time);

    longVersion = alloc(len);
    if (longVersion == NULL)
	longVersion = VIM_VERSION_LONG;
    else
	vim_snprintf(longVersion, len, msg,
		VIM_VERSION_LONG_ONLY, VIM_VERSION_DATE_ONLY, date_time);
}
# endif
#else
char	*longVersion = VIM_VERSION_LONG;

    void
init_longVersion(void)
{
    // nothing to do
}

/*
 * Place to put a short description when adding a feature with a patch.
 * Keep it short, e.g.,: "relative numbers", "persistent undo".
 * Also add a comment marker to separate the lines.
 * See the official Vim patches for the diff format: It must use a context of
 * one line only.  Create it by hand or use "diff -C2" and edit the patch.
 */
static char *(extra_patches[]) =
{   /* Add your patch description below this line */
/**/
    NULL
};

    int
highest_patch(void)
{
    // this relies on the highest patch number to be the first entry
    return included_patches[0];
}

#if defined(FEAT_EVAL)
/*
 * Return TRUE if patch "n" has been included.
 */
    int
has_patch(int n)
{
    int		h, m, l;

    // Perform a binary search.
    l = 0;
    h = (int)ARRAY_LENGTH(included_patches) - 1;
    for (;;)
    {
	m = (l + h) / 2;
	if (included_patches[m] == n)
	    return TRUE;
	if (l == h)
	    break;
	if (included_patches[m] < n)
	    h = m;
	else
	    l = m + 1;
    }
    return FALSE;
}
#endif

    void
ex_version(exarg_T *eap)
{
    /*
     * Ignore a ":version 9.99" command.
     */
    if (*eap->arg == NUL)
    {
	msg_putchar('\n');
	list_version();
    }
}

/*
 * Output a string for the version message.  If it's going to wrap, output a
 * newline, unless the message is too long to fit on the screen anyway.
 * When "wrap" is TRUE wrap the string in [].
 */
    static void
version_msg_wrap(char_u *s, int wrap)
{
    int		len = vim_strsize(s) + (wrap ? 2 : 0);

    if (!got_int && len < cmdline_width && msg_col + len >= cmdline_width
								&& *s != '\n')
	msg_putchar('\n');
    if (!got_int)
    {
	if (wrap)
	    msg_puts("[");
	msg_puts((char *)s);
	if (wrap)
	    msg_puts("]");
    }
}

    static void
version_msg(char *s)
{
    version_msg_wrap((char_u *)s, FALSE);
}

/*
 * List all features aligned in columns, dictionary style.
 */
    static void
list_features(void)
{
    list_in_columns((char_u **)features, -1, -1);
}

/*
 * List string items nicely aligned in columns.
 * When "size" is < 0 then the last entry is marked with NULL.
 * The entry with index "current" is inclosed in [].
 */
    void
list_in_columns(char_u **items, int size, int current)
{
    int		i;
    int		ncol;
    int		nrow;
    int		cur_row = 1;
    int		item_count = 0;
    int		width = 0;
#ifdef FEAT_SYN_HL
    int		use_highlight = (items == (char_u **)features);
#endif

    // Find the length of the longest item, use that + 1 as the column
    // width.
    for (i = 0; size < 0 ? items[i] != NULL : i < size; ++i)
    {
	int l = vim_strsize(items[i]) + (i == current ? 2 : 0);

	if (l > width)
	    width = l;
	++item_count;
    }
    width += 1;

    if (cmdline_width < width)
    {
	// Not enough screen columns - show one per line
	for (i = 0; i < item_count; ++i)
	{
	    version_msg_wrap(items[i], i == current);
	    if (msg_col > 0 && i < item_count - 1)
		msg_putchar('\n');
	}
	return;
    }

    // The rightmost column doesn't need a separator.
    // Sacrifice it to fit in one more column if possible.
    ncol = (cmdline_width + 1) / width;
    nrow = item_count / ncol + ((item_count % ncol) ? 1 : 0);

    // "i" counts columns then rows.  "idx" counts rows then columns.
    for (i = 0; !got_int && i < nrow * ncol; ++i)
    {
	int idx = (i / ncol) + (i % ncol) * nrow;

	if (idx < item_count)
	{
	    int last_col = (i + 1) % ncol == 0;

	    if (idx == current)
		msg_putchar('[');
#ifdef FEAT_SYN_HL
	    if (use_highlight && items[idx][0] == '-')
		msg_puts_attr((char *)items[idx], HL_ATTR(HLF_W));
	    else
#endif
		msg_puts((char *)items[idx]);
	    if (idx == current)
		msg_putchar(']');
	    if (last_col)
	    {
		if (msg_col > 0 && cur_row < nrow)
		    msg_putchar('\n');
		++cur_row;
	    }
	    else
	    {
		while (msg_col % width)
		    msg_putchar(' ');
	    }
	}
	else
	{
	    // this row is out of items, thus at the end of the row
	    if (msg_col > 0)
	    {
		if (cur_row < nrow)
		    msg_putchar('\n');
		++cur_row;
	    }
	}
    }
}

/*
 * Show the intro message when not editing a file.
 */
    void
maybe_intro_message(void)
{
    if (buf_is_empty(curbuf)

	    && vim_strchr(p_shm, SHM_INTRO) == NULL)

/*
 * Give an introductory message about Vim.
 * Only used when starting Vim on an empty file, without a file name.
 * Or with the ":intro" command (for Sven :-).
 */
    static void
intro_message(
    int		colon)		// TRUE for ":intro"
{
    int		i;
    int		row;
    int		blanklines;
    int		sponsor;
    char	*p;
    static char	*(lines[]) =
    {
	N_("VIM - Vi IMproved"),
	"",
	N_("version "),
	N_("by Bram Moolenaar et al."),
#ifdef MODIFIED_BY
	" ",
#endif
	N_("Vim is open source and freely distributable"),
	"",
	N_("Help poor children in Uganda!"),
	N_("type  :help Kuwasha<Enter>    for information "),
	"",
	N_("type  :q<Enter>               to exit         "),
	N_("type  :help<Enter>  or  <F1>  for on-line help"),
	N_("type  :help version9<Enter>   for version info"),
	NULL,
	"",
	N_("Running in Vi compatible mode"),
	N_("type  :set nocp<Enter>        for Vim defaults"),
	N_("type  :help cp-default<Enter> for info on this"),
    };
#ifdef FEAT_GUI
    static char	*(gui_lines[]) =
    {
	NULL,
	NULL,
	NULL,
	NULL,
# ifdef MODIFIED_BY
	NULL,
# endif
	NULL,
	NULL,
	NULL,
	N_("menu  Help->Orphans           for information    "),
	NULL,
	N_("Running modeless, typed text is inserted"),
	N_("menu  Edit->Global Settings->Toggle Insert Mode  "),
	N_("                              for two modes      "),
	NULL,
	NULL,
	NULL,
	N_("menu  Edit->Global Settings->Toggle Vi Compatible"),
	N_("                              for Vim defaults   "),
    };
#endif

    // blanklines = screen height - # message lines
    blanklines = (int)Rows - (ARRAY_LENGTH(lines) - 1);
    if (!p_cp)
	blanklines += 4;  // add 4 for not showing "Vi compatible" message

    // Don't overwrite a statusline.  Depends on 'cmdheight'.
    if (p_ls > 1)
	blanklines -= Rows - topframe->fr_height;
    if (blanklines < 0)
	blanklines = 0;

    // Show the sponsor and Uganda message two out of four times
    sponsor = (int)time(NULL);
    sponsor = ((sponsor & 2) == 0) - ((sponsor & 4) == 0);

    // start displaying the message lines after half of the blank lines
    row = blanklines / 2;
    if ((row >= 2 && topframe->fr_width >= 50) || colon)
    {
	for (i = 0; i < (int)ARRAY_LENGTH(lines); ++i)
	{
	    p = lines[i];
#ifdef FEAT_GUI
	    if (p_im && gui.in_use && gui_lines[i] != NULL)
		p = gui_lines[i];
#endif
	    if (p == NULL)
	    {
		if (!p_cp)
		    break;
		continue;
	    }
	    if (sponsor != 0)
	    {
		if (strstr(p, "children") != NULL)
		    p = N_("Sponsor Vim development!");
		else if (strstr(p, "Kuwasha") != NULL)
		    p = N_("type  :help sponsor<Enter>    for information ");
		else if (strstr(p, "Orphans") != NULL)
		    p = N_("menu  Help->Sponsor           for information    ");
	    }
	    if (*p != NUL)
		do_intro_line(row, (char_u *)_(p), i == 2, 0);
	    ++row;
	}
    }

    // Make the wait-return message appear just below the text.
    if (colon)
	msg_row = row;
}

    static void
do_intro_line(
    int		row,
    char_u	*mesg,
    int		add_version,
    int		attr)
{
    char_u	vers[20];
    int		col;
    char_u	*p;
    int		l;
    int		clen;
#ifdef MODIFIED_BY
# define MODBY_LEN 150
    char_u	modby[MODBY_LEN];

    if (*mesg == ' ')
    {
	vim_strncpy(modby, (char_u *)_("Modified by "), MODBY_LEN - 1);
	l = (int)STRLEN(modby);
	vim_strncpy(modby + l, (char_u *)MODIFIED_BY, MODBY_LEN - l - 1);
	mesg = modby;
    }
#endif

    // Center the message horizontally.
    col = vim_strsize(mesg);
    if (add_version)
    {
	STRCPY(vers, mediumVersion);
	if (highest_patch())
	{
	    // Check for 9.9x or 9.9xx, alpha/beta version
	    if (SAFE_isalpha((int)vers[3]))
	    {
		int len = (SAFE_isalpha((int)vers[4])) ? 5 : 4;
		sprintf((char *)vers + len, ".%d%s", highest_patch(),
							 mediumVersion + len);
	    }
	    else
		sprintf((char *)vers + 3, ".%d", highest_patch());
	}
	col += (int)STRLEN(vers);
    }
    col = (topframe->fr_width - col) / 2;
    if (col < 0)
	col = 0;

    // Split up in parts to highlight <> items differently.
    for (p = mesg; *p != NUL; p += l)
    {
	clen = 0;
	for (l = 0; p[l] != NUL
			 && (l == 0 || (p[l] != '<' && p[l - 1] != '>')); ++l)
	{
	    if (has_mbyte)
	    {
		clen += ptr2cells(p + l);
		l += (*mb_ptr2len)(p + l) - 1;
	    }
	    else
		clen += byte2cells(p[l]);
	}
	screen_puts_len(p, l, row, col + firstwin->w_wincol,
		*p == '<' ? HL_ATTR(HLF_8) : attr);
	col += clen;
    }

    // Add the version number to the version line.
    if (add_version)
	screen_puts(vers, row, col + firstwin->w_wincol, 0);
}

/*
 * ":intro": clear screen, display intro screen and wait for return.
 */
    void
ex_intro(exarg_T *eap UNUSED)
{
    screenclear();
#if defined(FEAT_TABPANEL)
    draw_tabpanel();
#endif
    intro_message(TRUE);
    wait_return(TRUE);
}

# Copy-on-write buffer snapshot upgrade

## Goal

Add a copy-on-write snapshot of buffer text.  A snapshot presents an immutable,
read-only view of one exact buffer revision and allows buffer queries to run
without blocking normal editing for the lifetime of the query.

The two non-negotiable goals are:

1. **Thread safety.** Snapshot queries must be safe from worker threads while
   the main thread edits, unloads, or deletes the originating buffer.  No
   snapshot reader may touch mutable `buf_T`, `memline_T`, memfile cache state,
   global editor state, or memory whose lifetime is controlled by the main
   thread.
2. **Low memory use.** Creating a snapshot must not copy the whole buffer.
   Snapshots share immutable storage with the live buffer, and editing copies
   only the smallest practical unit that is shared with a snapshot.

The snapshot interface is query-only.  It initially exposes line content, line
length, and line count.  It does not expose mutation, marks, options, undo,
windows, text properties, swap state, or callbacks.

This document is a design proposal.  The exact storage unit and synchronization
primitives must be validated with a prototype and measurements before the
public internal API is fixed.

## API shape

Names should follow the buffer interface added by the buffer upgrade:
`buf_line()`, `buf_line_len()`, and `buf_line_count()`.  The preferred API uses
an explicit, refcounted handle:

```c
typedef struct buf_snapshot buf_snapshot_T;

buf_snapshot_T *buf_snapshot_acquire(buf_T *buf);
void buf_snapshot_ref(buf_snapshot_T *snapshot);
void buf_snapshot_unref(buf_snapshot_T *snapshot);

varnumber_T buf_snapshot_tick(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot);
const char_u *buf_snapshot_line(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot,
                                linenr_T lnum);
colnr_T buf_snapshot_line_len(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot,
                              linenr_T lnum);
linenr_T buf_snapshot_line_count(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot);
```

Conceptually, a caller asking for revision `tick` performs:

```c
snapshot = buf_snapshot_acquire(buf);
tick = buf_snapshot_tick(snapshot);
line = buf_snapshot_line(snapshot, lnum);
```

This provides the intended equivalent of
`snapshot_line(buf, tick, lnum)` and `snapshot_line_count(buf, tick)`, but does
not make `(buf, tick)` the ownership token.  A bare tick is an identity, not a
lifetime guarantee.  Looking up a snapshot by `(buf, tick)` and returning a
pointer would race with buffer deletion or release of the final snapshot
reference.  It would also require a retained per-buffer revision registry,
which increases memory use.

If lookup by tick is later required, make acquisition explicit and fallible:

```c
buf_snapshot_T *buf_snapshot_acquire_tick(int fnum, varnumber_T tick);
```

That function must return a referenced handle or `NULL`; query functions still
operate on the handle.  Do not accept a raw `buf_T *` from a worker thread.
The first implementation should omit this registry until a real consumer needs
it.

### Contract

- `buf_snapshot_acquire()` is called on the main editor thread.  It captures the
  current text revision and returns one owned reference, or `NULL` on failure.
- `buf_snapshot_ref()`, `buf_snapshot_unref()`, and all query functions are
  safe on any thread.
- A snapshot remains valid after its source buffer is edited, unloaded, or
  deleted.
- `buf_snapshot_tick()` identifies the captured text revision.  The initial
  implementation may use `CHANGEDTICK(buf)`, but publication must ensure the
  tick and root describe the same committed revision.
- Query functions perform no allocation, locking, I/O, swap-file access,
  message emission, callback, or lazy cache fill.
- A line pointer is immutable and remains valid until the caller releases its
  snapshot reference.  Multiple line pointers from one snapshot may be held at
  once; unlike `buf_line()`, a later query does not invalidate an earlier one.
- Line bytes are NUL-terminated.  `buf_snapshot_line_len()` excludes the NUL.
  Embedded NUL representation must match the buffer interface contract.
- The initial API returns text only.  It must not expose packed text-property
  bytes.  Supporting properties later requires a separate typed query.
- Valid line numbers are `1` through `buf_snapshot_line_count(snapshot)`.
  Invalid input returns `NULL` for a line and `0` for its length, without using
  Vim's global error machinery.
- An unloaded buffer cannot produce a new snapshot.  Existing snapshots remain
  valid.  Vim's one-empty-line representation is preserved.
- Snapshot functions are observational only and never increment changedtick.

`const` prevents accidental writes through the API but is not the thread-safety
mechanism.  Immutability, ownership, and publication are.

## Proposed representation

Use a persistent tree whose leaves contain immutable line records.  A snapshot
handle owns a reference to one immutable root:

```c
struct buf_snapshot
{
    snapshot_node_T *bs_root;
    linenr_T         bs_line_count;
    varnumber_T      bs_tick;
    snapshot_ref_T   bs_refcount;
};
```

The exact fields remain private.  `snapshot_ref_T` represents a portable
reference-count implementation selected for Vim's supported platforms; it is
not a proposed concrete typedef.

### Immutable line records

A line record contains its byte length and NUL-terminated bytes in one
allocation where practical.  Records are immutable once published and may be
shared by the live revision and any number of snapshots.  Length is stored so
queries never call `STRLEN()`.

Do not create one allocation per line during conversion if that causes
unacceptable overhead.  Prefer immutable leaf slabs containing a bounded group
of line offsets and bytes.  The prototype should compare:

- fixed-size leaf slabs;
- size-bounded leaves, split when edited; and
- reuse of existing memline data blocks after separating mutable cache state
  from immutable payload.

The last option is likely lowest-memory, but only if block locking, swap-file
translation, encryption, and cache eviction are completely absent from the
reader path.

### Persistent index

Interior nodes store subtree line counts, allowing line lookup and total count
without mutable side tables.  The live buffer owns one root.  A snapshot is
normally O(1): increment the root reference and allocate only the small handle.

On append, replace, or delete, mutation uses path copying:

1. Build replacement leaf data without changing published storage.
2. Copy only nodes on the path from the changed leaf to the root.
3. Reuse and reference unchanged children.
4. Publish the fully initialized new root.
5. Release the live buffer's reference to the old root.

Readers that hold the old root continue to see the old revision.  Cost should
be O(log n) index nodes plus changed line/leaf bytes, not O(number of snapshots)
and not O(buffer size).

### What happens when a line is edited

The old line is not copied into a separate snapshot at edit time.  It is already
part of an immutable leaf owned by the currently published revision.  A
snapshot has retained that revision, and therefore retains the old leaf.

For example, replacing line 120 follows this sequence on the main thread:

1. Resolve line 120 to immutable leaf `A` in revision `R1`.
2. Allocate leaf `B` and copy the line table and bytes from `A`, applying the
   replacement while constructing `B`.  Neither `A` nor `R1` is modified.
3. Allocate copies of the interior nodes between `A` and the root.  Point the
   copied path at `B` and share all unaffected subtrees.
4. Construct revision `R2` with the new root, updated line count if needed, and
   the new tick.
5. After memline, undo, and other required mutation bookkeeping succeeds,
   atomically publish `R2` as the live revision.
6. Release the live reference to `R1`.  Snapshot references keep `R1`, `A`, and
   its old line 120 alive.  Without a snapshot, unreferenced old nodes are freed.

Thus "copy on write" means **copy the shared leaf before changing it**, not
"save the old line into every snapshot."  There is one old leaf regardless of
how many snapshots share that revision.  If a live leaf is proven uniquely
owned it is still preferable initially to construct a replacement leaf: never
mutating published storage makes the thread-safety invariant auditable.  A
future unique-owner optimization is allowed only before publication and only
if it cannot race with snapshot acquisition.

Insert and delete use the same rule.  They may split or merge leaves and update
subtree line counts, but published leaves and nodes remain unchanged.

### Relationship to memline blocks

Vim's buffer is already managed in memline data and pointer blocks, but those
blocks are not currently safe snapshot objects.  They participate in a mutable
cache and may be locked, translated, evicted, loaded from swap, encrypted, or
changed in place.  A worker snapshot must not invoke any of those mechanisms.

The snapshot should be block-based as well, because copying one allocation per
line or the whole buffer would waste memory.  However, snapshot **leaf slabs**
should initially be a separate immutable abstraction, not raw memline blocks.
They may use similar size targets and may eventually share an immutable payload
with memline after cache and swap metadata are separated from text storage.

Using exactly the same block boundaries is not required and may be harmful:

- memline block size is driven by swap and cache behavior;
- copy-on-write size is driven by edit amplification and retained memory;
- a one-byte edit should not preserve or copy an unnecessarily large block;
- a very long line must be represented without imposing a huge normal leaf
  size; and
- insertions should split leaves without renumbering or copying unrelated text.

The initial recommendation is a size-bounded leaf slab containing multiple
whole lines, offsets, lengths, and packed text bytes.  Target a small bounded
payload, permit an oversize leaf for one long line, and split a leaf when an
edit exceeds the target.  The prototype must determine the target size; it
should not simply inherit the memline block size without measurements.

Leaf size is the main memory/performance tuning decision.  Copying an entire
large memline block for a one-byte edit may retain too much old text; very small
leaves increase index and allocation overhead.  Measure realistic editing,
large files, long lines, and many retained snapshots before selecting it.

## Thread-safety model

Thread safety is an unbreakable invariant, not a best-effort property.

### Main-thread ownership

Only the main editor thread may:

- acquire a snapshot from `buf_T`;
- mutate or publish the live root;
- interact with memline, memfile, swap files, undo, text properties, changed
  state, autocommands, or global Vim state.

Worker threads receive only referenced `buf_snapshot_T *` handles.  They must
never receive `buf_T *` for snapshot access.

### Publication

All nodes and line storage are fully initialized before they become reachable
from a published root.  Publishing a root uses release semantics; acquiring or
referencing a published snapshot uses matching acquire semantics.  Published
nodes are never modified.

A new root and its tick form one revision.  Mutation must not expose the new
root with the old tick or vice versa.  Prefer constructing a revision object
that contains both and atomically publishing one pointer rather than publishing
fields independently.

### Reclamation

Reference counting is the initial reclamation strategy because snapshots have
explicit lifetimes and Vim already has many reference-counted objects.  A node
or slab is freed only after the live revision and every snapshot that can reach
it have released their references.

The implementation must use real atomic reference operations when references
cross threads.  `volatile`, the current `buf_T` lock fields, and assumptions
about word-sized writes are not synchronization.  If Vim cannot provide the
required atomics on a supported target, snapshot worker-thread support must be
compile-time unavailable there; it must not silently become unsafe.

Recursive destruction can overflow the C stack or create a long pause when the
last large snapshot is released.  Use iterative release or bounded tree depth,
and permit final reclamation to be queued to the main thread if platform
allocators are not safe to call from workers.  Queueing must not require the
source buffer to remain alive.

### No hidden mutable state

Snapshot queries cannot call `buf_line()`, `ml_get_buf()`, or any helper that
locks blocks, updates a cached line, reads a swap file, reports an error, or
consults `curbuf`.  Thread sanitizers and code review should treat any such call
as a correctness failure.

## Integration with the buffer interface

The live buffer interface remains the sole mutation boundary:

```c
buf_append_line(...)
buf_replace_line(...)
buf_delete_line(...)
```

Initially, these operations should update memline and the persistent snapshot
representation in one main-thread transaction.  They publish a new snapshot
revision only after the mutation succeeds.  On failure, neither the published
root nor its tick changes.

This dual representation is suitable for proving the API but may temporarily
increase memory use.  The end state should make the persistent immutable text
store the buffer's canonical payload, with memline reduced or adapted to swap,
recovery, and compatibility responsibilities.  Keeping two permanent complete
copies would violate the low-memory goal.

Every mutation path must pass through the buffer interface before snapshots
can be declared correct.  Existing internal memline mutations and writable
`buf_line(..., TRUE)` access are blockers because they can bypass copy-on-write
and revision publication.  The buffer-interface enforcement tool should gain a
snapshot mode that rejects bypasses outside explicitly reviewed internals.

Undo is not automatically a snapshot implementation.  Undo entries encode
changes and may be pruned, are tied to mutable buffer state, and are not a
thread-safe random-access text store.  Shared immutable text records may later
be reused by both systems, but their ownership contracts stay separate.

## Memory policy

- Snapshot creation is O(1) apart from the handle.
- Unchanged text and index nodes are shared across revisions.
- Mutation copies only the changed immutable leaf and its index path.
- No retained global `(buffer, tick)` registry in the initial implementation.
- No line copy on query and no per-query allocation.
- Cache values must either be immutable and stored in nodes, or thread-local;
  there is no mutable shared line cache.
- Empty leaves and underfull neighboring leaves may be merged during later
  mutations, never by changing a published node.
- Add accounting for bytes retained solely by snapshots.  This is diagnostic
  data, not an automatic eviction mechanism: a live referenced snapshot cannot
  be invalidated to save memory.
- Allocation failure while editing must preserve the old live revision and
  existing snapshots.  The mutation reports failure through the existing
  buffer API; partial trees are released.

## Phased implementation

### Phase 0: settle invariants and measure

- [x] Inventory every text mutation, including writable cached-line access and
  memline-internal paths.
- [x] Define the representative memory and edit benchmark matrix that must be
  implemented with the prototype before choosing leaf size.
- [x] Audit existing atomic/refcount facilities and define the portability
  requirement and unsupported-build behavior.
- [x] Audit changedtick and decide whether it identifies snapshot revisions.

#### Phase 0 findings

The existing `tools/check_internal_mutations.py` inventory is the baseline.
`internal_mutations.txt` currently reports 171 raw findings across nine files:
44 implicit mutations, 17 explicit/internal mutations, one writable line
access, and 109 direct memline state mutations.  It reports no line-pointer
follow-up candidates.  Most findings are memline implementation internals or
comments/prototypes, but the writable cached-line path in `memline.c` proves
that successful snapshot publication cannot yet be attached only to
`buf_append_line()`, `buf_replace_line()`, and `buf_delete_line()`.

`b:changedtick` is not the snapshot revision.  Normal text notification
increments it, but bulk low-level mutations may be grouped under one increment,
undo may increment it more than once, and `unchanged()` increments it for
modified-state and write transitions that do not change text.  Buffer load,
recovery, and deletion also affect it.  A snapshot revision therefore has its
own monotonically increasing per-buffer sequence, incremented exactly once
when a new immutable text root is published.  A snapshot may retain the source
changedtick for diagnostics or conservative invalidation, but must not expose
it as its canonical revision identity.

Vim has no reusable portable atomic or mutex abstraction.  Existing Vim object
reference counts are plain `int` and are main-thread/re-entrancy mechanisms,
not cross-thread synchronization.  Windows code provides `Interlocked*`
precedents, but core configure support does not currently detect C11 atomics,
compiler atomic builtins, or general pthread synchronization.  A plain Vim
refcount, `volatile`, or `sig_atomic_t` is forbidden for snapshots.

Before Phase 1 exposes cross-thread retain/release, add a small private
snapshot-atomic portability layer with:

- acquire/release pointer publication;
- atomic increment and decrement with safe final-release semantics;
- a Windows `Interlocked*` backend;
- configure-tested compiler/C11 backends where available; and
- compile-time disabling of worker-thread snapshots on legacy targets where no
  correct backend exists.

A main-thread-only correctness prototype may use ordinary ownership internally,
but it must not claim thread safety or publish the API to workers until this
layer exists.  A mutex fallback is acceptable only after Vim gains reliable
thread-library detection and linkage; Python-specific `-pthread` flags are not
sufficient.

#### Phase 0 status

Phase 0 design and source audits are complete.  Phase 1 begins with two
implementation prerequisites: the private atomic portability layer and a
benchmark harness capable of reporting snapshot-owned/retained bytes.  Leaf
size remains intentionally undecided until prototype measurements exist.

### Phase 1: immutable prototype

- [x] Add a private snapshot handle and immutable, size-bounded leaf slabs.
- [x] Add a sorted immutable leaf index with binary-search line lookup.  Replace
  it with the persistent tree when Phase 2 adds path-copying mutations.
- [x] Build a snapshot from a loaded buffer with a one-time full copy.  This is
  a correctness prototype only, not completion of the low-memory goal.
- [x] Add line, line-length, line-count, revision, and allocated-size queries.
- [x] Add focused integration coverage through the private `test_getvalue()`
  test hook, including empty and oversized-leaf lines.
- [ ] Add the portable atomic reference implementation and concurrent
  reference/final-release tests.  Current `ref`/`unref` operations and snapshot
  acquisition are main-thread-only.
- [ ] Add a real internal consumer after atomic ownership is available; the
  test hook copies results and does not expose snapshot handles.
- [ ] Add allocation-failure coverage and direct C tests for pointer lifetime
  across source edits, unload, and wipeout.
- [x] Verify query implementations use only immutable snapshot storage.  The
  acquisition path alone reads through the buffer interface.

#### Phase 1 implementation status

`src/buffer_snapshot.c` implements the mirror prototype using a 4 KiB
experimental leaf target.  Each leaf owns line offsets, stored lengths, and
packed NUL-terminated text.  A line larger than the target receives its own
oversized leaf.  The snapshot owns a sorted leaf-pointer array and line lookup
uses binary search.  Snapshot construction allocates an upper-bound pointer
array of one pointer per source line; Phase 2 should replace this prototype
tradeoff with incrementally allocated persistent index nodes.

The buffer carries `b_snapshot_revision`, currently initialized to zero.  It is
intentionally not derived from `b:changedtick`.  Phase 2 must increment it once
per successfully published immutable text root before the revision value is
meaningful to consumers.

The snapshot query path is immutable, allocation-free, and independent of
memline.  The handle lifetime is not yet cross-thread-safe because the current
reference count is a plain main-thread counter.  Passing these handles to
workers before the atomic item above is completed is prohibited.

### Phase 2: copy-on-write live revisions

- Route append, replace, and delete through persistent path copying.
- Publish root and tick as one revision after successful mutation.
- Keep memline behavior, undo, swap, recovery, properties, and diagnostics
  unchanged while cross-checking both representations in debug/test builds.
- Remove the one-time full copy from snapshot acquisition.

### Phase 3: close mutation bypasses

- Eliminate or encapsulate writable `buf_line(..., TRUE)` access.
- Require all text mutations to update the canonical revision through the
  buffer API.
- Extend interface enforcement and run a full-source audit.
- Define behavior for load, reload, unload, wipeout, recovery, and buffer
  replacement.

### Phase 4: consolidate storage

- Avoid permanent duplicate text ownership between memline and snapshot
  storage.
- Reuse immutable payload in swap/recovery where safe, or make memline consume
  the persistent store through a private adapter.
- Tune leaf sizing, tree fanout, release batching, and allocator overhead from
  measurements.

### Phase 5: enable worker consumers

- Enable only after sanitizer and stress validation.
- Pass referenced snapshot handles through worker queues.
- Document cancellation and ownership at each consumer.
- Keep all result application and buffer mutation on the main thread, checking
  that the originating buffer/revision is still relevant before applying a
  result.

## Tests and validation

### Functional tests

- Snapshot empty, one-line, multiline, very-long-line, and unloaded buffers.
- Retain a snapshot across append, replace, delete, undo, redo, reload, unload,
  and wipeout; verify the old text and count never change.
- Hold pointers to several snapshot lines and verify later queries and live
  edits do not invalidate them.
- Verify invalid line numbers and allocation failures have deterministic,
  callback-free results.
- Verify text-property mutations do not corrupt text snapshots and are not
  exposed as line bytes.
- Compare every snapshot line and length against the captured live revision in
  debug tests.

### Concurrency tests

- Many readers query the same snapshot while the main thread repeatedly edits
  and publishes revisions.
- Readers retain and release different generations while the buffer is
  unloaded and deleted.
- Race final `unref` operations from multiple workers.
- Run supported configurations under ThreadSanitizer and AddressSanitizer.
- Add deterministic stress hooks around publication and final reference drops,
  rather than relying only on timing-sensitive tests.

### Memory and performance tests

The benchmark harness must run the same workloads against the pre-snapshot
baseline and candidate leaf payload targets, initially 1, 4, 16, and 64 KiB.
Use deterministic generated buffers and report wall time, allocations,
snapshot-owned bytes, bytes retained solely by old revisions, and peak resident
memory where the platform can provide it.

Required datasets are:

- 100,000 short lines of 20 bytes;
- 100,000 medium lines of 200 bytes;
- a mixed source-like distribution;
- 1,000 lines of 1 MiB each; and
- a single line larger than every candidate leaf target.

Required workloads are:

- acquire and release 1, 10, and 1,000 snapshots without edits;
- replace one byte repeatedly in the same line;
- replace one byte in uniformly random lines;
- append and delete 10,000 lines at the start, middle, and end;
- retain 1, 10, and 100 generations while sparse edits continue;
- sequentially scan every line and perform one million random line queries;
  and
- release the final snapshot retaining a large old revision.

Measure and verify:

- snapshot acquisition remains O(1) versus buffer size;
- retained bytes are proportional to changed leaves and copied index paths;
- many snapshots of one revision do not duplicate text storage;
- very long lines do not force the normal leaf target to grow;
- insert/delete throughput in hot editing paths remains acceptable;
- query functions perform no allocation; and
- final release has bounded stack usage and acceptable latency.

A full-buffer copy on every snapshot, one complete tree per snapshot, or
unbounded revision retention fails the design regardless of functional test
results.

## Completion criteria

The upgrade is complete only when:

- snapshot acquisition shares the current immutable root and does not copy all
  text;
- snapshot queries are read-only, callback-free, allocation-free, and safe on
  worker threads;
- a snapshot survives edits, unload, and deletion of its source buffer;
- all text mutations participate in copy-on-write publication;
- returned line pointers remain valid for the snapshot lifetime;
- atomic publication and reclamation are validated on every enabled platform;
- focused buffer, undo, recovery, swap, text-property, and scripting tests
  pass;
- concurrency stress plus available thread/address sanitizer runs pass; and
- measured memory retention and editing overhead are acceptable and documented.

Thread safety takes precedence over API convenience and performance.  Low
memory use takes precedence over retaining a historical revision registry.
Neither goal may be weakened silently for a supported build.

" Tests for Vim buffer

" Test for the :bunload command with an offset
func Test_bunload_with_offset()
  %bwipe!
  call writefile(['B1'], 'Xb1', 'D')
  call writefile(['B2'], 'Xb2', 'D')
  call writefile(['B3'], 'Xb3', 'D')
  call writefile(['B4'], 'Xb4', 'D')

  " Load four buffers. Unload the second and third buffers and then
  " execute .+3bunload to unload the last buffer.
  edit Xb1
  new Xb2
  new Xb3
  new Xb4

  bunload Xb2
  bunload Xb3
  exe bufwinnr('Xb1') . 'wincmd w'
  .+3bunload
  call assert_equal(0, getbufinfo('Xb4')[0].loaded)
  call assert_equal('Xb1',
        \ fnamemodify(getbufinfo({'bufloaded' : 1})[0].name, ':t'))

  " Load four buffers. Unload the third and fourth buffers. Execute .+3bunload
  " and check whether the second buffer is unloaded.
  ball
  bunload Xb3
  bunload Xb4
  exe bufwinnr('Xb1') . 'wincmd w'
  .+3bunload
  call assert_equal(0, getbufinfo('Xb2')[0].loaded)
  call assert_equal('Xb1',
        \ fnamemodify(getbufinfo({'bufloaded' : 1})[0].name, ':t'))

  " Load four buffers. Unload the second and third buffers and from the last
  " buffer execute .-3bunload to unload the first buffer.
  ball
  bunload Xb2
  bunload Xb3
  exe bufwinnr('Xb4') . 'wincmd w'
  .-3bunload
  call assert_equal(0, getbufinfo('Xb1')[0].loaded)
  call assert_equal('Xb4',
        \ fnamemodify(getbufinfo({'bufloaded' : 1})[0].name, ':t'))

  " Load four buffers. Unload the first and second buffers. Execute .-3bunload
  " from the last buffer and check whether the third buffer is unloaded.
  ball
  bunload Xb1
  bunload Xb2
  exe bufwinnr('Xb4') . 'wincmd w'
  .-3bunload
  call assert_equal(0, getbufinfo('Xb3')[0].loaded)
  call assert_equal('Xb4',

  call assert_fails(',100bunload', 'E16:')

  call assert_fails('$bunload', 'E90:')
endfunc

" Test for :buffer, :bnext, :bprevious, :brewind, :blast and :bmodified
" commands
func Test_buflist_browse()
  %bwipe!
  call assert_fails('buffer 1000', 'E86:')

  call writefile(['foo1', 'foo2', 'foo3', 'foo4'], 'Xbrowse1', 'D')
  call writefile(['bar1', 'bar2', 'bar3', 'bar4'], 'Xbrowse2', 'D')
  call writefile(['baz1', 'baz2', 'baz3', 'baz4'], 'Xbrowse3', 'D')
  edit Xbrowse1
  let b1 = bufnr()
  edit Xbrowse2
  let b2 = bufnr()
  edit +/baz4 Xbrowse3
  let b3 = bufnr()

  call assert_fails('buffer ' .. b1 .. ' abc', 'E488:')
  call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(4, line('.'))
  exe 'buffer +/bar2 ' .. b2
  call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(2, line('.'))
  exe 'buffer +/bar1'
  call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(1, line('.'))

  brewind +
  call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(4, line('.'))

  blast +/baz2
  call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(2, line('.'))

  bprevious +/bar4
  call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(4, line('.'))

  bnext +/baz3
  call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(3, line('.'))

  call assert_fails('bmodified', 'E84:')
  call setbufvar(b2, '&modified', 1)
  exe 'bmodified +/bar3'
  call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  call assert_equal(3, line('.'))

  " With no listed buffers in the list, :bnext and :bprev should fail
  %bwipe!
  set nobuflisted
  call assert_fails('bnext', 'E85:')
  call assert_fails('bprev', 'E85:')
  set buflisted

  call assert_fails('sandbox bnext', 'E48:')

  %bwipe!
endfunc

" Test for :bnext and :bprev when called from help and non-help buffers.
func Test_bnext_bprev_help()
  %bwipe!

  e XHelp1 | set bt=help
  let b1 = bufnr()
  e Xbuf1
  let b2 = bufnr()

  " There's only one buffer of each type.
  b XHelp1
  bnext | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  b Xbuf1
  bnext | call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())

  " Add one more buffer of each type.
  e XHelp2 | set bt=help
  let b3 = bufnr()
  e Xbuf2
  let b4 = bufnr()

  " Help buffer jumps to help buffer.
  b XHelp1
  bnext | call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  bnext | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())

  " Regular buffer jumps to regular buffer.
  b Xbuf1
  bnext | call assert_equal(b4, bufnr())
  bnext | call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b4, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b2, bufnr())

  " :brewind and :blast are not affected by the buffer type.
  b Xbuf2
  brewind | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  b XHelp1
  blast   | call assert_equal(b4, bufnr())

  " Cycling through help buffers works even if they aren't listed.
  b XHelp1
  setlocal nobuflisted
  bnext | call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  bnext | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  setlocal nobuflisted
  bprev | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())
  bprev | call assert_equal(b3, bufnr())
  bnext | call assert_equal(b1, bufnr())

  %bwipe!
endfunc

  new Xbuf2
  let cmd = "exe 'bdel ' .. bufnr('Xbuf2') .. ' xxx ' .. bufnr('Xbuf1')"
  call assert_fails(cmd, 'E94:')
  call assert_equal(2, winnr('$'))
  call assert_equal(1, getbufinfo('Xbuf1')[0].loaded)
  call assert_equal(0, getbufinfo('Xbuf2')[0].loaded)

  %bwipe!
endfunc

" Test for editing another buffer from a modified buffer with :confirm
func Test_goto_buf_with_confirm()
  CheckUnix
  CheckNotGui
  CheckFeature dialog_con
  " When dialog_con_gui is defined, Vim is compiled with GUI support
  " and FEAT_BROWSE will be defined, which causes :confirm :b to
  " call do_browse(), which will try to use a GUI file browser,
  " which aborts if a GUI is not available.
  CheckNotFeature dialog_con_gui
  new XgotoConf
  enew
  call setline(1, 'test')
  call assert_fails('b XgotoConf', 'E37:')
  call feedkeys('c', 'L')
  call assert_fails('confirm b XgotoConf', 'E37:')
  call assert_true(&modified)
  call assert_true(empty(bufname('%')))
  call feedkeys('y', 'L')
  confirm b XgotoConf
  call assert_equal('XgotoConf', bufname('%'))
  call assert_equal(['test'], readfile('Untitled'))
  e Untitled
  call setline(2, 'test2')
  call feedkeys('n', 'L')
  confirm b XgotoConf
  call assert_equal('XgotoConf', bufname('%'))
  call assert_equal(['test'], readfile('Untitled'))
  call delete('Untitled')
  close!
endfunc

" Test for buffer match URL(scheme) check
" scheme is alpha and inner hyphen only.
func Test_buffer_scheme()
  CheckMSWindows

  set noswapfile
  set noshellslash
  %bwipe!
  let bufnames = [
    \ #{id: 'ssb0', name: 'test://xyz/foo/ssb0'    , match: 1},
    \ #{id: 'ssb1', name: 'test+abc://xyz/foo/ssb1', match: 0},
    \ #{id: 'ssb2', name: 'test_abc://xyz/foo/ssb2', match: 0},
    \ #{id: 'ssb3', name: 'test-abc://xyz/foo/ssb3', match: 1},
    \ #{id: 'ssb4', name: '-test://xyz/foo/ssb4'   , match: 0},
    \ #{id: 'ssb5', name: 'test-://xyz/foo/ssb5'   , match: 0},
    \]
  for buf in bufnames
    new `=buf.name`
    if buf.match
      call assert_equal(buf.name,    getbufinfo(buf.id)[0].name)
    else
      " slashes will have become backslashes
      call assert_notequal(buf.name, getbufinfo(buf.id)[0].name)
    endif
    bwipe
  endfor

  set shellslash&
  set swapfile&
endfunc

" Test for buffer allocation failure
func Test_buflist_alloc_failure()
  %bw!

  edit XallocFail1
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('edit XallocFail2', 'E342:')

  " test for bufadd()
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('call bufadd("Xbuffer")', 'E342:')

  " test for setting the arglist
  edit XallocFail2
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('next XallocFail3', 'E342:')

  " test for setting the alternate buffer name when writing a file
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('write Xother', 'E342:')
  call delete('Xother')

  " test for creating a buffer using bufnr()
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails("call bufnr('Xnewbuf', v:true)", 'E342:')

  " test for renaming buffer using :file
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('file Xnewfile', 'E342:')

  " test for creating a buffer for a popup window
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('call popup_create("mypop", {})', 'E342:')

  if has('terminal')
    " test for creating a buffer for a terminal window
    call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
    call assert_fails('call term_start(&shell)', 'E342:')
    %bw!
  endif

  " test for loading a new buffer after wiping out all the buffers
  edit XallocFail4
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('%bw!', 'E342:')

  " test for :checktime loading the buffer
  call writefile(['one'], 'XallocFail5', 'D')
  if has('unix')
    edit XallocFail5
    " sleep for some time to make sure the timestamp is different
    sleep 200m
    call writefile(['two'], 'XallocFail5')
    set autoread
    call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
    call assert_fails('checktime', 'E342:')
    set autoread&
    bw!
  endif

  " test for :vimgrep loading a dummy buffer
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('vimgrep two XallocFail5', 'E342:')

  " test for quickfix command loading a buffer
  call test_alloc_fail(GetAllocId('newbuf_bvars'), 0, 0)
  call assert_fails('cexpr "XallocFail6:10:Line10"', 'E342:')
endfunc

func Test_closed_buffer_still_in_window()
  %bw!

  let s:fired = 0
  let s:w = win_getid()
  new
  let s:b = bufnr()
  setl bufhidden=wipe
  augroup ViewClosedBuffer
    autocmd!
    autocmd BufUnload * ++once let s:fired += 1 | call assert_fails(
          \ 'call win_execute(s:w, "' .. s:b .. 'buffer")', 'E1546:')
  augroup END
  quit!
  " Previously resulted in s:b being curbuf while unloaded (no memfile).
  call assert_equal(1, s:fired)
  call assert_equal(1, bufloaded(bufnr()))
  call assert_equal(0, bufexists(s:b))
  %bw!

  new flobby
  let s:w = win_getid()
  let s:b = bufnr()
  setl bufhidden=wipe
  augroup ViewClosedBuffer
    autocmd!
    autocmd BufUnload * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| wincmd p
          \| call assert_notequal(s:w, win_getid())
          \| call assert_notequal(s:b, bufnr())
          \| execute s:b 'sbuffer'
          \| call assert_equal(s:w, win_getid())
          \| call assert_equal(s:b, bufnr())
  augroup END
  " Not a problem if 'switchbuf' switches to an existing window instead.
  set switchbuf=useopen
  quit!
  call assert_equal(2, s:fired)
  call assert_equal(0, bufexists(s:b))
  set switchbuf&
  %bw!

  edit floob
  let s:b = bufnr()
  enew
  augroup ViewClosedBuffer
    autocmd!
    autocmd BufWipeout * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_fails(s:b .. 'sbuffer | wincmd p', 'E1546:')
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$')) " :sbuffer shouldn't have split.
  augroup END
  " Used to be a heap UAF.
  execute s:b 'bwipeout!'
  call assert_equal(3, s:fired)
  call assert_equal(0, bufexists(s:b))
  %bw!

  edit flarb
  let s:b = bufnr()
  enew
  let b2 = bufnr()
  augroup ViewClosedBuffer
    autocmd!
    autocmd BufWipeout * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_fails(s:b .. 'sbuffer', 'E1159:')
  augroup END
  " :sbuffer still should fail if curbuf is closing, even if it's not the target
  " buffer (as switching buffers can fail after the split)
  bwipeout!
  call assert_equal(4, s:fired)
  call assert_equal(0, bufexists(b2))
  %bw!

  let s:w = win_getid()
  split
  new
  let s:b = bufnr()
  augroup ViewClosedBuffer
    autocmd!
    autocmd BufWipeout * ++once let s:fired += 1 | call win_gotoid(s:w)
          \| call assert_fails(s:b .. 'buffer', 'E1546:') | wincmd p
  augroup END
  bw! " Close only this buffer first; used to be a heap UAF.
  call assert_equal(5, s:fired)

  unlet! s:w s:b s:fired
  autocmd! ViewClosedBuffer
  %bw!
endfunc

" Cursor position should be restored when switching to a buffer previously
" viewed in a window, regardless of whether it's visible in another one.
func Test_switch_to_previously_viewed_buffer()
  set nostartofline
  new Xviewbuf
  call setline(1, range(1, 200))
  let oldwin = win_getid()
  vsplit

  call cursor(100, 3)
  call assert_equal('100', getline('.'))
  edit Xotherbuf
  buffer Xviewbuf
  call assert_equal([0, 100, 3, 0], getpos('.'))
  call assert_equal('100', getline('.'))

  edit Xotherbuf
  wincmd p
  normal! gg10dd
  wincmd p
  buffer Xviewbuf
  call assert_equal([0, 90, 3, 0], getpos('.'))
  call assert_equal('100', getline('.'))

  edit Xotherbuf
  wincmd p
  normal! ggP
  wincmd p
  buffer Xviewbuf
  call assert_equal([0, 100, 3, 0], getpos('.'))
  call assert_equal('100', getline('.'))

  edit Xotherbuf
  wincmd p
  normal! 96gg10ddgg
  wincmd p
  buffer Xviewbuf
  " The original cursor line was deleted, so cursor is restored to the start
  " of the line before the deleted range.
  call assert_equal([0, 95, 1, 0], getpos('.'))
  call assert_equal('95', getline('.'))

  normal! u
  exe win_id2win(oldwin) .. 'close'
  setlocal bufhidden=hide

  call cursor(200, 3)
  call assert_equal('200', getline('.'))
  edit Xotherbuf
  buffer Xviewbuf
  call assert_equal([0, 200, 3, 0], getpos('.'))
  call assert_equal('200', getline('.'))

  bwipe! Xotherbuf
  bwipe! Xviewbuf
  set startofline&
endfunc

func Test_bdelete_skip_closing_bufs()
  set hidden
  let s:fired = 0

  edit foo
  edit bar
  let s:next_new_bufnr = bufnr('$') + 1
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Only window and other buffer is closing.
    " No choice but to switch to a new, empty buffer.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('bar', bufname())
          \| bdelete
          \| call assert_equal('', bufname())
          \| call assert_equal(s:next_new_bufnr, bufnr())
  augroup END
  bdelete foo
  call assert_equal(1, s:fired)
  unlet! s:next_new_bufnr
  %bw!

  edit baz
  edit bar
  edit fleb
  edit foo
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Only window, au_new_curbuf is NOT closing; should end up there.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('foo', bufname())
          \| bwipeout
          \| call assert_equal('bar', bufname())
  augroup END
  buffer baz
  buffer foo
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd BufLeave * ++once ++nested bdelete baz
  augroup END
  edit bar
  call assert_equal(2, s:fired)
  %bw!

  edit baz
  edit bar
  edit fleb
  edit foo
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Like above, but au_new_curbuf IS closing.
    " Should use the most recent jumplist buffer instead.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('foo', bufname())
          \| bwipeout
          \| call assert_equal('baz', bufname())
  augroup END
  buffer baz
  buffer foo
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd BufLeave * ++once ++nested bdelete bar
  augroup END
  edit bar
  call assert_equal(3, s:fired)
  %bw!

  edit foo
  edit floob
  edit baz
  edit bar
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Only window, most recent buffer in jumplist is closing.
    " Should switch to the next most-recent buffer in the jumplist instead.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('bar', bufname())
          \| bdelete
          \| call assert_equal('floob', bufname())
  augroup END
  buffer baz
  buffer floob
  buffer foo
  buffer bar
  bdelete foo
  call assert_equal(4, s:fired)
  %bw!

  edit foo
  edit baz
  edit bar
  edit floob
  edit bazinga
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Only window, most recent jumplist buffer is gone, next most-recent is
    " closing.  Should switch to the 3rd most-recent jumplist buffer.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('bar', bufname())
          \| bwipeout
          \| call assert_equal('baz', bufname())
  augroup END
  buffer bazinga
  buffer baz
  buffer floob
  buffer foo
  buffer bar
  noautocmd bdelete foo
  bdelete floob
  call assert_equal(5, s:fired)
  %bw!

  edit foo
  edit baz
  edit floob
  edit bazinga
  edit bar
  augroup SkipClosing
    autocmd!
    " Like above, but jumplist cleared, no next buffer in the buffer list and
    " previous buffer is closing.  Should switch to the buffer before previous.
    autocmd BufDelete * ++once let s:fired += 1
          \| call assert_equal(1, winnr('$'))
          \| call assert_equal('bar', bufname())
          \| bunload
          \| call assert_equal('floob', bufname())
  augroup END
  buffer bazinga
  buffer baz
  buffer floob
  buffer foo
  buffer bar
  noautocmd bdelete foo
  clearjumps
  bdelete bazinga
  call assert_equal(6, s:fired)

  unlet! s:fired
  autocmd! SkipClosing
  set hidden&
  %bw!
endfunc

Implemented the Phase 1 immutable snapshot prototype.

### Implementation

Added `src/buffer_snapshot.c` with:

- `buf_snapshot_acquire()`
- `buf_snapshot_ref()` / `buf_snapshot_unref()`
- `buf_snapshot_tick()`
- `buf_snapshot_line()`
- `buf_snapshot_line_len()`
- `buf_snapshot_line_count()`
- `buf_snapshot_size()`

Snapshot representation:

- Experimental 4 KiB immutable leaf slabs.
- Packed NUL-terminated line bytes.
- Stored offsets and lengths.
- Oversized dedicated leaves for long lines.
- Sorted leaf index with binary-search lookup.
- Stable line pointers for the snapshot lifetime.
- No allocation, memline access, or global state access during queries.

This is currently a full immutable mirror constructed from the live buffer. Copy-on-write sharing begins in Phase 2.

### Integration

- Added the opaque `buf_snapshot_T` declaration and `b_snapshot_revision` to `src/structs.h`.
- Added generated `src/proto/buffer_snapshot.pro`.
- Integrated the new source into Unix, Windows, Cygwin/MinGW, Amiga, and VMS builds.
- Added patch entry `1003` to `src/version.c`.
- Added a private test bridge through `test_getvalue('buf_snapshot')`.
- Added empty, multiline, empty-line, and 5,000-byte long-line coverage in `src/testdir/test_buffer.vim`.
- Updated `upgrades/buffer-snapshot/UPGRADE.md` with Phase 1 status and remaining work.

### Important limitation

Snapshot acquisition and reference management remain **main-thread-only** because the portable atomic layer is not implemented yet. Immutable queries themselves touch only snapshot storage, but handles must not be passed to workers until atomic ownership is complete.

`b_snapshot_revision` is initialized to zero. It deliberately does not use `b:changedtick`; Phase 2 will advance it when publishing immutable roots.

### Validation

Passed:

- `make -C src proto`
- `make -C src -j2`
- `make -C src/testdir test_buffer.res`
- `python3 tools/check_buffer_interface.py --all`
- `git diff --check`

The next Phase 1 work is the atomic reference layer, direct pointer-lifetime tests, allocation-failure coverage, and a real internal consumer.

The allocator audit shows final worker release cannot blindly use Vim’s general allocation path under every build (`MEM_PROFILE` and global exit state are relevant). I’ll therefore gate cross-thread capability explicitly: atomic retain/release is enabled only on supported compiler/Windows backends and reported unavailable for unsafe configurations, while unsupported builds retain main-thread behavior rather than pretending to be thread-safe.

/* vi:set ts=8 sts=4 sw=4 noet:
 *
 * VIM - Vi IMproved	by Bram Moolenaar
 *
 * Do ":help uganda"  in Vim to read copying and usage conditions.
 * Do ":help credits" in Vim to see a list of people who contributed.
 * See README.txt for an overview of the Vim source code.
 */

/*
 * buffer_snapshot.c: immutable, read-only buffer snapshots.
 *
 * This is the Phase 1 mirror implementation.  Snapshot construction and
 * reference management are main-thread-only until Vim has a portable atomic
 * reference-count implementation.  Queries touch only immutable memory.
 */

#include "vim.h"

#define SNAPSHOT_LEAF_TARGET 4096

#if defined(MSWIN)
typedef volatile LONG snapshot_ref_T;
# define SNAPSHOT_ATOMIC_REFS
#elif defined(__clang__) || (defined(__GNUC__) \
	&& (__GNUC__ > 4 || (__GNUC__ == 4 && __GNUC_MINOR__ >= 7)))
typedef int snapshot_ref_T;
# define SNAPSHOT_ATOMIC_REFS
#else
typedef int snapshot_ref_T;
#endif

typedef struct
{
    linenr_T	sl_first;
    linenr_T	sl_count;
    size_t	sl_data_size;
    size_t	*sl_offsets;
    colnr_T	*sl_lengths;
    char_u	*sl_data;
} snapshot_leaf_T;

struct buf_snapshot
{
    snapshot_ref_T	bs_refcount;
    varnumber_T		bs_revision;
    linenr_T		bs_line_count;
    int			bs_leaf_count;
    snapshot_leaf_T	**bs_leaves;
    size_t		bs_allocated;
};

/*
 * Free a snapshot leaf.
 */
    static void
snapshot_leaf_free(snapshot_leaf_T *leaf)
{
    if (leaf == NULL)
	return;
    vim_free(leaf->sl_offsets);
    vim_free(leaf->sl_lengths);
    vim_free(leaf->sl_data);
    vim_free(leaf);
}

/*
 * Free an unreferenced snapshot.
 */
    static void
snapshot_free(buf_snapshot_T *snapshot)
{
    int i;

    if (snapshot == NULL)
	return;
    for (i = 0; i < snapshot->bs_leaf_count; ++i)
	snapshot_leaf_free(snapshot->bs_leaves[i]);
    vim_free(snapshot->bs_leaves);
    vim_free(snapshot);
}

/*
 * Build one immutable leaf starting at "first".  Set "next" to the first line
 * not included in the leaf.
 */
    static snapshot_leaf_T *
snapshot_leaf_build(buf_T *buf, linenr_T first, linenr_T line_count,
	linenr_T *next)
{
    snapshot_leaf_T	*leaf;
    linenr_T		lnum;
    linenr_T		count = 0;
    size_t		data_size = 0;
    size_t		offset = 0;

    for (lnum = first; lnum <= line_count; ++lnum)
    {
	colnr_T len = buf_line_len(buf, lnum);
	size_t needed = (size_t)len + 1;

	if (count > 0 && data_size + needed > SNAPSHOT_LEAF_TARGET)
	    break;
	if (data_size + needed < data_size)
	    return NULL;
	data_size += needed;
	++count;
    }

    leaf = alloc_clear_id(sizeof(snapshot_leaf_T), aid_buf_snapshot);
    if (leaf == NULL)
	return NULL;
    leaf->sl_offsets = alloc_clear_id(
				(size_t)count * sizeof(size_t), aid_buf_snapshot);
    leaf->sl_lengths = alloc_clear_id(
				(size_t)count * sizeof(colnr_T), aid_buf_snapshot);
    leaf->sl_data = alloc_clear_id(data_size, aid_buf_snapshot);
    if (leaf->sl_offsets == NULL || leaf->sl_lengths == NULL
							|| leaf->sl_data == NULL)
    {
	snapshot_leaf_free(leaf);
	return NULL;
    }

    leaf->sl_first = first;
    leaf->sl_count = count;
    leaf->sl_data_size = data_size;
    for (lnum = first; lnum < first + count; ++lnum)
    {
	linenr_T index = lnum - first;
	colnr_T len = buf_line_len(buf, lnum);
	char_u *line = buf_line(buf, lnum, FALSE);

	leaf->sl_offsets[index] = offset;
	leaf->sl_lengths[index] = len;
	mch_memmove(leaf->sl_data + offset, line, (size_t)len + 1);
	offset += (size_t)len + 1;
    }

    *next = first + count;
    return leaf;
}

/*
 * Capture the current text of "buf" in immutable storage.
 * Must be called on the main editor thread.
 */
    buf_snapshot_T *
buf_snapshot_acquire(buf_T *buf)
{
    buf_snapshot_T	*snapshot;
    linenr_T		lnum;
    linenr_T		line_count;
    int			leaf_count = 0;

    if (buf == NULL || !buf_is_loaded(buf))
	return NULL;

    line_count = buf_line_count(buf);
    snapshot = alloc_clear_id(sizeof(buf_snapshot_T), aid_buf_snapshot);
    if (snapshot == NULL)
	return NULL;
    snapshot->bs_leaves = alloc_clear_id(
		(size_t)line_count * sizeof(snapshot_leaf_T *), aid_buf_snapshot);
    if (snapshot->bs_leaves == NULL)
    {
	vim_free(snapshot);
	return NULL;
    }

    lnum = 1;
    while (lnum <= line_count)
    {
	snapshot_leaf_T *leaf = snapshot_leaf_build(buf, lnum, line_count,
								&lnum);

	if (leaf == NULL)
	{
	    snapshot->bs_leaf_count = leaf_count;
	    snapshot_free(snapshot);
	    return NULL;
	}
	snapshot->bs_leaves[leaf_count++] = leaf;
    }

    snapshot->bs_refcount = 1;
    snapshot->bs_revision = buf->b_snapshot_revision;
    snapshot->bs_line_count = line_count;
    snapshot->bs_leaf_count = leaf_count;
    snapshot->bs_allocated = sizeof(*snapshot)
			+ (size_t)line_count * sizeof(snapshot_leaf_T *);
    for (int i = 0; i < leaf_count; ++i)
	snapshot->bs_allocated += sizeof(snapshot_leaf_T)
		+ (size_t)snapshot->bs_leaves[i]->sl_count
					* (sizeof(size_t) + sizeof(colnr_T))
		+ snapshot->bs_leaves[i]->sl_data_size;
    return snapshot;
}

/*
 * Return TRUE when snapshot references may cross threads in this build.
 * MEM_PROFILE makes Vim's allocation accounting unsuitable for worker-thread
 * final release, even when atomic counters are available.
 */
    int
buf_snapshot_threadsafe(void)
{
#if defined(SNAPSHOT_ATOMIC_REFS) && !defined(MEM_PROFILE)
    return TRUE;
#else
    return FALSE;
#endif
}

/*
 * Add a reference to "snapshot".
 */
    void
buf_snapshot_ref(buf_snapshot_T *snapshot)
{
    if (snapshot == NULL)
	return;
#if defined(MSWIN)
    (void)InterlockedIncrement(&snapshot->bs_refcount);
#elif defined(SNAPSHOT_ATOMIC_REFS)
    (void)__atomic_add_fetch(&snapshot->bs_refcount, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
#else
    ++snapshot->bs_refcount;
#endif
}

/*
 * Drop a reference to "snapshot" and free it after the final release.
 */
    void
buf_snapshot_unref(buf_snapshot_T *snapshot)
{
    int is_last;

    if (snapshot == NULL)
	return;
#if defined(MSWIN)
    is_last = InterlockedDecrement(&snapshot->bs_refcount) == 0;
#elif defined(SNAPSHOT_ATOMIC_REFS)
    is_last = __atomic_sub_fetch(&snapshot->bs_refcount, 1,
							__ATOMIC_ACQ_REL) == 0;
#else
    is_last = --snapshot->bs_refcount == 0;
#endif
    if (is_last)
	snapshot_free(snapshot);
}

/*
 * Return the immutable text revision captured by "snapshot".
 */
    varnumber_T
buf_snapshot_tick(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot)
{
    return snapshot == NULL ? 0 : snapshot->bs_revision;
}

/*
 * Return the number of lines in "snapshot".
 */
    linenr_T
buf_snapshot_line_count(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot)
{
    return snapshot == NULL ? 0 : snapshot->bs_line_count;
}

/*
 * Find the leaf containing "lnum".
 */
    static snapshot_leaf_T *
snapshot_find_leaf(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot, linenr_T lnum)
{
    int low = 0;
    int high = snapshot->bs_leaf_count - 1;

    while (low <= high)
    {
	int middle = low + (high - low) / 2;
	snapshot_leaf_T *leaf = snapshot->bs_leaves[middle];

	if (lnum < leaf->sl_first)
	    high = middle - 1;
	else if (lnum >= leaf->sl_first + leaf->sl_count)
	    low = middle + 1;
	else
	    return leaf;
    }
    return NULL;
}

/*
 * Return an immutable line.  The pointer remains valid until the caller drops
 * its snapshot reference.
 */
    const char_u *
buf_snapshot_line(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot, linenr_T lnum)
{
    snapshot_leaf_T *leaf;
    linenr_T index;

    if (snapshot == NULL || lnum < 1 || lnum > snapshot->bs_line_count)
	return NULL;
    leaf = snapshot_find_leaf(snapshot, lnum);
    if (leaf == NULL)
	return NULL;
    index = lnum - leaf->sl_first;
    return leaf->sl_data + leaf->sl_offsets[index];
}

/*
 * Return a snapshot line length, excluding the terminating NUL.
 */
    colnr_T
buf_snapshot_line_len(const buf_snapshot_T *snapshot, linenr_T lnum)
{
    snapshot_leaf_T *leaf;
